author: nonretail_writer
central_thesis: A front-end-led global policy pivot (US 2Y +36 bps over twenty observations in a bear flattening, the Bank of England's hike to 0.5% and Lagarde no longer ruling out a 2022 ECB hike) is colliding with a data-ownership divide in mega-cap earnings, epitomised by Meta Platforms (FB)'s record one-day wipeout against Alphabet's and Amazon's cloud/search strength; the edition therefore favours cash-generative energy, asset-sensitive banks and pricing-power staples over long-duration, ad-dependent growth, and treats the January payrolls report, Russia's Belarus drills and China's post-holiday reopening strictly as pending risks.
sources_policy: Every fact comes from a 2022-02-04 frozen-feed headline cited with its ID in the same part, or from the 2022-02-04 market card (Treasury block and instrument rows, each quoted with its own completed session and tagged accordingly). The exclusions file for this date is empty. Each ID is used at most twice (262 distinct IDs, 290 citations), leaving room for the separate retail section within the merged cap of four. No other date's feed, card, spec, draft or note was used. Process disclosure: during the first card read, a generic scratchpad file was overwritten mid-read by another agent's process, and fragments of other dates' cards were briefly displayed. They were discarded unused. The 2022-02-04 card and digest were then re-run into date-specific files, and a final re-run showed them byte-identical to the working copies. Cited titles were checked directly against feeds/2022-02-04 via the verifier's loader. No numeric spot-FX is quoted; the DXY is used as an index. Currency direction (zloty, euro) appears only where a dated headline reports it. Previews (Olympic opening times, the payrolls Omicron warning, Uber, Amazon consensus) are used only to establish pending events or expectations, never outcomes. After-hours reactions to the 3 February Amazon, Pinterest, Snap and Ford results are described only with headline wording (soar, dazzle, skid), because the card's 2022-02-03 closes predate those releases. verify.py --nonretail: PASS, 0 FAIL, 0 WARN, 8,995 body words; all block ranges in bounds.
known_ambiguities_omitted: Toshiba $1 billion power-chip investment (n1473, Reuters, stamped 2022-02-03): possibly a Tokyo-morning 4 February announcement carried on a day-granular stamp (Asian-morning after-cutoff risk); omitted.

U.S. to Deploy 3,000 Troops to Romania, Poland, Germany (n1493): the source metadata names an anachronistic 'U.S. Department of War (.gov)', which cannot be attributed cleanly in a February 2022 edition; replaced with Sky News (n1491) and ABC (n1487) without the 3,000 figure.
Putin-Xi meeting and joint statement (4 February): pending, with no own-date preview headline in the feed; not mentioned.

RBA Statement on Monetary Policy (4 February 00:30 UTC): after the cutoff, with no own-date preview; not mentioned. Only the 1 February decision statement and Lowe's 'rates will go up' remarks are used (n0036 is stamped 1 February and may refer to the 2 February address; it predates the cutoff either way and is used undated).

Beijing Olympic opening (4 February) and the US January payrolls (4 February 13:30 UTC): treated only as pending, via the opening-time preview n0200 and the White House warning n2022; no outcomes and no dates or times asserted.

Super Bowl LVI (13 February): only the pre-event ad sell-out (n0105) is used; the game, ads and app outages are unknown. Southwest's Feb. 16 alcohol return (n0866) is a future-dated item and is not used.

Spot-FX: Polish rate-card headlines with numeric zloty levels (n1587, n1625, n1672, n1673, n1674) and the numeric grosze move in n1714 are not quoted. n1629 and n1714 are used for direction only, and the EUR/USD recovery headline (n1251) only for 'high eurozone inflation'. Sterling headlines (n0097, n1283) are not used numerically.

Contradictory Meta value-loss figures ($230bn Forbes n0808, $232bn CNBC n1141, $237bn CBS n0868, nearly $240bn Business Insider n1149, $251bn Bloomberg n0838): only CNBC's figure is quoted, with attribution.
Amazon advertising run-rate: CNBC $31bn (n1128) vs GeekWire $30bn (n1144). Only CNBC's figure is quoted, attributed.

AMD 'AMD's 2022 Sales Hit $21.5 Billion' (n1040) is ambiguous between guidance and actual sales; it is quoted as the outlet's headline wording and paired with CNBC's 'strong 2022 sales outlook', never presented as reported revenue.

Pinterest active users (n1156, Social Media Today, stamped 3 February) may have been published on the US evening. It describes the 3 February after-close release, which predates the cutoff, so it is kept for that content only.

Caixin January PMI (n0144) is stamped 29 January, although the release may have come on 30 January. It predates the cutoff either way; used without a release date. 'Official' is not asserted for n0148.
'Bank of England raises rates by most since 1995' (n1260): ambiguous wording about the size and sequence of the move; not used. n1259, n1262, n1257 and n1310 carry the hike facts instead.

Promotional, sensational or misdated items not used: 'Expert Warns of 41% Drop in S&P 500' (n0360), 'Bitcoin Price Predictions for 2025' (n0528), Chainers NFT promotion (n0959), Catecoin (n0902), the misdated 'List of Fake Crypto Websites 2023' (n0906), 'Christian-Screened Stocks to Research in 2026' (n0223) and 'Employee Legal Awareness Day — February 13, 2027' (n2010).
Card levels marked 'withheld' (Comcast, GE, Western Digital) are not quoted. Only GE's percentage change was considered, and it was not used.

The footwear sell-off headline (n1728) does not name the company, so it is reported only as 'a footwear heavyweight'. n1730 (new investor at a Biedronka/Lidl rival) is ambiguous about the company and is not used.
